newsitem.title: USA: Zilog in merger pact with Texas Pacific.
newsitem.headline: Zilog in merger pact with Texas Pacific.

text.p: Zilog Inc, a leading semiconductor manufacturer, said Monday it had signed a defintive agreement to be acquired by Texas Pacific Group, a private investment partnership, for $25 a share in a deal valued at about $527 million.

Under the agreement, holders of Zilog can elect to retain their Zilog shares or receive $25 cash per share. Zilog said that in no event can more than 400,000 common shares of Zilog, or about 2 percent of the total outstanding, be retained by current shareholders.

It said Warburg, Pincus Capital Co LP and related affiliates, currently Zilog's largest shareholder, have committed to retain up to 400,000 shares, ensuring that all other shareholders who do not elect to retain their shares will receive $25 cash per share.

To the extent that other shareholders also elect to retain shares, the 400,000 shares available to be retained will be prorated among all shareholders electing to retain, and cash will be paid for all other shares, it said.
The merger is intended to be treated as a recapitalization for accounting purposes, it said.
Following the merger, TPG will own about 90 percent of Zilog's voting common stock, and the shares to be retained will represent the remaining 10 percent, it said.
In addition, TPG will own non-voting common stock that will increase its overall economic interest in Zilog to about 93.3 percent,
The shares to be retained will have an economic interest of about 6.7 percent. It is not expected that Zilog will have publicly listed shares following the merger.
It said the Zilog board has unanimously approved the merger agreement.
The merger is subject to completion of financing, and approval by Zilog shareholders and regulators. It is expected to be consummated early in the fourth quarter.
Warburg has agreed to vote its shares, which represent approximately 27 percent of Zilog's current shares outstanding, in favor of the merger, it added.
